world.title: Donald Trump loses US Congress; Netanyahu faces deadlock at home: What happens to Iran war now?
world.summary: Donald Trump lost control of Congress following a significant Democratic victory, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces political deadlock amid ongoing challenges. Both leaders are grappling with the implications of the unresolved conflict with Iran, which has influenced their electoral outcomes. The political setbacks raise questions about future strategies regarding the Iran war for both nations.

world.title: Iran allows Indian ships free passage through Strait of Hormuz amid tensions
world.summary: Iran has lifted transit restrictions for vessels from India, China, Iraq, and Qatar in the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian lawmaker stated that this decision aligns with Tehran's mutual interests, particularly regarding medicine imports from India and political support from China. The move reflects Iran's strategic partnerships amid ongoing regional tensions and aims to facilitate trade.

world.title: U.S. midterm results may matter less for India-U.S. ties than for India’s room to manoeuvre in geopolitics
world.summary: The U.S. midterm results are expected to have a limited impact on India-U.S. bilateral relations, focusing instead on broader geopolitical implications. Issues such as the Iran war, Russian oil, trade discussions, and the Quad alliance will shape India's strategic options. The elections may strengthen the Democrats, influencing the global operating environment for India more than direct ties with the U.S.

business.title: Sebi eases digital KYC rules for NRIs, foreign nationals from December 3
business.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will permit Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs), and foreign nationals from FATF-compliant countries to complete their Know Your Customer (KYC) processes digitally starting December 3. This change aims to simplify the onboarding process and facilitate investment in Indian markets for these individuals.

business.title: Stock Market Close: Sensex rises for 5th day, gains 384 pts; Nifty at 23,961; IT only sectoral loser
business.summary: The Sensex increased by 384 points, marking its fifth consecutive day of gains, while the Nifty reached 23,961. In broader markets, the Nifty MidCap 100 rose by 1.55%, and the Nifty SmallCap 100 gained 2.0%. The IT sector was the only sector to decline during this trading session. Overall, market sentiment remained positive across most sectors.

technology.title: Why BIM Still Doesn't Know What Your Building Is Made Of
technology.summary: Acelab's Material Intelligence Model aims to enhance architectural design efficiency by integrating connected material data. Currently, changing a material in Revit requires teams to revert to specifications, spreadsheets, and drawings to ensure consistency, unlike moving a wall, which automatically updates all related plans and sections. This highlights ongoing challenges in building information modeling (BIM) regarding material identification.

technology.title: Galaxy A26, Galaxy A27 One UI 9.0 update reaches the US
technology.summary: Samsung has begun rolling out the One UI 9.0 (Android 17) update for the Galaxy A26 and Galaxy A27 in the United States. The update is initially available for factory-unlocked variants of both models. Users can expect new features and improvements with this update, enhancing the overall performance and user experience of the devices.

technology.title: Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 Ad Takes a Bold Swipe at Apple's iPhone Duo
technology.summary: Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 advertisement critiques Apple's iPhone Duo by showcasing a cracked screen as a reason to switch. The ad emphasizes Samsung's confidence and humor, aiming to redefine the competition in the foldable phone market. It suggests that consumers prioritize user experience over specifications when comparing devices, highlighting the ease of use of the Galaxy Z Fold8.

sports.title: 'Imagine The Red Ball': Sunil Gavaskar Left Stunned By Arshdeep Singh's Swing
sports.summary: Sunil Gavaskar has expressed admiration for Arshdeep Singh's bowling skills, particularly his ability to swing the ball in both directions. Gavaskar considers this talent a significant asset, suggesting it positions Singh as a strong candidate for red-ball cricket. His comments highlight the challenges batters face when confronting such versatile bowling, emphasizing Singh's potential in the longer format of the game.

sports.title: OFFICIAL: Real Madrid announce tennis legend Rafa Nadal as a member of the Board of Directors
sports.summary: Real Madrid has officially announced tennis legend Rafa Nadal as a member of its Board of Directors. This decision was made during a meeting of the Board on November 4. Nadal, known for his exceptional career in tennis, will now play a role in the governance of the football club, marking a notable crossover between sports.

sports.title: 'He was annoying': Jacob Duffy's hilarious take on Virat Kohli after India's Auckland victory
sports.summary: New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy humorously commented on Virat Kohli following India's victory in Auckland. Duffy described Kohli as "annoying" after the Indian batting star's performance in the match. Kohli's dismissal was marked by him throwing his bat in the air, highlighting his frustration. The exchange reflects the competitive spirit and camaraderie between players from both teams.

health.title: Italy’s repatriation detention centers under medical scanner
health.summary: Italy's repatriation detention centers, known as Centri di Permanenza per il Rimpatrio (CPRs), are under scrutiny for their health and medical-ethical implications. These facilities, which detain foreign nationals awaiting removal, have garnered attention following a July 2025 investigation that was made public in February 2026. The focus highlights the need for more comprehensive analysis beyond migration policy debates.

health.title: Drug-free diabetes implant offers ‘promising’ future for patients, say scientists
health.summary: A wireless electronic implant developed by bioengineers at ETH Zurich may provide a drug-free method to manage type 2 diabetes and obesity. The device works by directly clearing excess glucose from the bloodstream. Researchers describe the findings as promising, potentially offering a new treatment option that eliminates the need for traditional medications or insulin for patients.

health.title: DUSP4 protein identified as key to preventing CAR T cell exhaustion
health.summary: Researchers have identified the DUSP4 protein as crucial for preventing exhaustion in CD8+ T cells within the tumor microenvironment. Enhancing DUSP4 activity improves the efficacy of engineered CAR T cells against colorectal cancer. This discovery may lead to new strategies for optimizing T-cell therapies, potentially increasing their effectiveness in combating this type of cancer.

science.title: NASA's Voyager 1 nears historic milestone: It will soon be one light-day away from Earth
science.summary: NASA's Voyager 1, launched nearly 50 years ago, is nearing a significant milestone, becoming one light-day away from Earth, over 16 billion miles distant. As it ventures deeper into space, engineers face challenges including declining power, aging equipment, and unexpected communication disruptions. This milestone highlights the remarkable journey of humanity's most distant spacecraft and its operational difficulties.

science.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
science.summary: NASA is working to save the Hubble Space Telescope from a potential fall to Earth by 2033 or 2034. The agency has issued a Request for Information to private space companies, seeking innovative solutions to boost Hubble's orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or ensure its safe disposal. This effort aims to extend Hubble's operational life beyond its current limitations.

science.title: Finding the right rhythm to free droplets stuck in narrow pores
science.summary: Simulations reveal that intermediate frequency pulsations effectively mobilize droplets trapped in narrow pores. This discovery could enhance fluid transport in subsurface reservoirs, which are underground formations containing oil, natural gas, water, or carbon dioxide. The findings address challenges posed by capillary forces that can immobilize droplets within porous materials, potentially improving extraction and management of these valuable resources.

entertainment.title: 'I'll Never Cheat You': Abhijeet Bhattacharya Slams Lip-Syncing After Daler Mehndi Controversy
entertainment.summary: Singer Abhijeet Bhattacharya criticized lip-syncing during live performances, asserting his commitment to singing live regardless of his vocal quality. His remarks followed a controversy involving fellow artist Daler Mehndi. During a recent performance in Chhattisgarh, Bhattacharya emphasized that he would always perform authentically, stating, "No matter how I sing, I will sing live."

entertainment.title: 'Ramayana' producer Namit Malhotra confirms the second part is delayed to 2028, says the Ranbir Kapoor starrer could become a trilogy: 'We need to do justice for a film of this size'
entertainment.summary: Namit Malhotra, producer of 'Ramayana: Part 1', confirmed that the second part is delayed until 2028. He mentioned that the film, starring Ranbir Kapoor, might evolve into a trilogy to ensure the story receives proper treatment. 'Ramayana: Part 1' is set to release in theaters on November 5, ahead of the anticipated sequels.

entertainment.title: In 2009, Michael Jackson left a trust for his three children; 17 years later, daughter Paris is asking a court to move $600 million into it, while estate executors say unresolved tax litigation preven
entertainment.summary: Seventeen years after Michael Jackson's death, his daughter Paris Jackson has requested a court to transfer $600 million into a trust established for her and her siblings. The estate's executors argue that ongoing tax litigation prevents the transfer. This legal move raises concerns regarding the inheritance of Paris and her brothers from their father's estate.
